title: CV and Website Maintainer
text:
What it is
CV and Website Maintainer is a plugin for Codex, with Claude Code support in progress. A plugin is a set of instructions the assistant reads when a task calls for them, so it works the same way every time. This one keeps an academic’s records (appointments, grants, talks, abstracts, teaching, mentoring, media and more) in structured files, and builds a Word CV and a Quarto website from them. Publications come from Zotero.
You ask in plain words (“Add this teaching session and these slides”, “Check for possible updates”, “Help me start from my CV”) and the assistant follows the plugin’s steps. You don’t need to edit YAML or run commands yourself.
It was previously called Academic Records. Its internal name is still academic-records, so existing setups keep working.

title: CV and Website Maintainer
text:
What it does







You want to
The plugin




Start from a CV, an existing website or nothing
Stages candidate records privately for your review, and can set up a starter website and Word CV


Set preferences or resume setup
Asks one question at a time and saves answers in private storage outside your website


Add or correct an activity
Shows the exact change to your records and saves it only after you approve


Find possible new activities
Searches only the sources you approved (such as PubMed or your email) and lists candidates for review


Add publications
Adds approved references to Zotero through a separate Zotero integration


Hand an update to another chat
Prepares the request without claiming it was saved

title: CV and Website Maintainer
section: What it won’t do without you
text:
What it won’t do without you

Save without approval. Every change to your records is shown exactly, and saved only once you approve it.
Publish on its own. Saving a record doesn’t rebuild your CV or publish your website; those steps follow the permissions you set.
Handle patient information. If slides or files may contain patient identifiers, it warns you and stops before copying or linking them.

title: CV and Website Maintainer
text:
Status

Codex: the supported host. To install, follow the installation guide.
Claude Code: support is in progress and not yet released.
Testing: an automated test suite runs on every change; blind testing with simulated users is planned. See How it’s tested.

Source, history and issues are on GitHub.

title: Sites built with it
text:
Written for version 0.2.0.

Vagish Hemmige: academic website and CV. Its records are kept in YAML with this plugin; the website and the CV PDF are built from them. Source on GitHub.

If you have built a site with the plugin, open an issue on the plugin’s repository with its address.

title: How it’s tested
text:
Automated tests
The repository has 626 automated tests in its tests folder. They run on made-up records and check the plugin’s helpers: approvals before saving, backups and receipts, detecting a file changed since it was proposed, privacy checks before publishing, and the CV and website outputs. 61 of them are skipped unless the tools they need, such as R, Quarto or Git, are available. Pushing to GitHub and Office file conversion are mocked, not run for real.
These tests check the helpers, not how the assistant behaves with a real person.

title: How it’s tested
text:
Blind testing (planned)
The next step is testing with simulated users who don’t see the plugin’s instructions or the answers. Six made-up academics, from a senior physician who has never used R to an experienced website owner, each ask for help in their own words, and a separate evaluator checks the actual files, not the conversation. One of them starts with no website at all.
The plan is in issues #1 and #2 and draft pull request #3. No runs have been done yet. Results will be posted here.
